correctness.rationale: Antipodal pairing converts squared geodesic distance exactly into pi^2/4+E phi((x·V)^2), phi(s)=arcsin^2 sqrt(s). Its Taylor recurrence a_(n+1)=2n² a_n/((n+1)(2n+1)) has positive coefficients, a2=1/3, hence phi is 2/3-strongly convex on [0,1], and isotropy gives E Z=1/d. Equality in strict Jensen is Z constant. For Rademacher cube vertices E Z²=(3-2 sum x_i^4)/d²; for cross-polytope Z=x_i² uniformly. Their variances vanish only at coordinate axes and the all-equal-absolute-coordinate cube vertices, respectively, and these attain baseline. Independently verified 490 numerical stability inequalities over d=2..8. The proof is analytic for all integers d>=2, samples are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: The fully read 2018 primary paper on Fréchet means is an algorithm on S² for arbitrary finite data, not an exact dimension-free bound for antipodal isotropic measures or the cross-dual complete argmin formula. Hotz–Huckemann addresses circle intrinsic means, and Roychowdhury quantization centers; no mathematical implication from inspected results yields the fourth-moment stability and equality rigidity. Generic Jensen alone leaves a nontrivial tight equality-class characterization.
residual_risks: Earlier spherical potential-theory or tight-frame energy inequalities may yield the same result through a dual formulation.
Hotz–Huckemann and recent spherical quantization works were not all read in full; abstract-level inspection cannot exclude hidden equivalent special configurations.

value.rationale: Nonconvex geodesic Fréchet minimization on spheres has useful exact special configurations. A dimension-uniform sharp lower bound under isotropy, equality characterization and complete cube/cross-polytope minimizers (with quantitative stability) provide natural explicit benchmarks for spherical statistics and symmetric designs, beyond a single numerical example.

final_claim: Every antipodal isotropic probability on S^{d-1} has F_mu(x)>=pi^2/4+arcsin^2(1/sqrt d)+(1/3)(E(x·V)^4-1/d^2), with sharp equality iff |x·V|=1/sqrt d almost surely; the cube and cross-polytope vertex measures have precisely the dual vertex minimizer sets and explicit fourth-moment stability gaps.
limitations: Requires exact antipodal isotropy and intrinsic angular squared distance; stability coefficients valid but not asserted optimal.
Universal convexity proof, not finite experiments, establishes the all-dimensional theorem.
